notEstablished.revitalisation: Not established from the sources consulted. The Education Law (Art. 44) makes Lao language and Lao script the official languages for teaching and learning, and Art. 45 covers only foreign languages, naming no ethnic-group language and no measure to maintain one; the UNESCO GEM Report PEER inclusion profile's section on ethnic and language groups records only extending distance learning for minority groups and teaching Lao as a second language to ethnic minority children, with the official national language remaining the medium of instruction. Neither document names a body, a date or any funding for reversing language shift.

Not established from the sources consulted. Art. 16 of the 2004 Constitution obliges the state to design and apply effective programs to foster and develop all languages of Afghanistan, but names no programme, body, start date or funding; the UNESCO GEM Report PEER inclusion profile for Afghanistan records only that school books are produced in two national languages and in several minority languages, and it describes the framework as it stood before August 2021.
